Affiliation:: University of Oklahoma and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
Application Areas: Human-Centric Visual Analytics and Cognitive Psychology
Interactive Multidimensional Data Exploration and Dimensionality Reduction
Temporal Data Visualization and Time Series Analysis
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Empirical Validation of Perceptual Limits: Quantifying human cognitive constraints in visual encoding to establish evidence-based design heuristics, demonstrated through user studies and categorical encoding assessments showing performance decline beyond six categories.

Interactive Structural Correction in Projections: Developing algorithmic interventions to mitigate topological distortions in dimensionality reduction, specifically using Distortion-aware Brushing to correct Missing and False Neighbors during cluster analysis.

Signal Processing for Temporal Clarity: Applying mathematical filtering and layout strategies to manage data density in time series, utilizing techniques like LOESS regression, FFT, and Trellis/Spiral chart layouts to enhance trend identification and prediction accuracy.

Noise-Resilient Feature Prioritization: Investigating human-centric strategies for distinguishing signal from noise in complex datasets, employing Visual Stenography and free-form sketching to analyze how users prioritize semantic features under varying Signal-to-Noise Ratios.
Summary Description: Ghulam Quadri specializes in Human-Computer Interaction and Visual Analytics, bridging cognitive psychology with interactive data visualization. His research investigates cognitive biases in dimensionality reduction and graphical perception in categorical data. By employing user studies and crowdsourced experiments, he quantifies how System 1/2 processing affects visual accuracy. He empirically validates design heuristics, demonstrating performance declines beyond six categories. His work expands into interactive techniques for Multidimensional Projections, developing 'Distortion-aware Brushing' to correct structural distortions. He also addresses dense temporal data, evaluating static density-reduction strategies to optimize trend identification. Most recently, he introduced 'Visual Stenography,' using free-form sketching to analyze how noise influences feature prioritization. His work integrates psychological theories and algorithmic interventions to develop empirically grounded guidelines, ensuring visual analytics tools support accurate, reliable scientific discovery.
